2.artifact: Your team norms and role assignments — each norm written as a specific, observable "We will…" commitment.
2.reflect: How would an observer know, just by watching a meeting, whether your team is keeping each norm?
2.proves: Norms are specific and measurable — not vague values, and not busywork.

5.artifact: The one essential standard you chose, plus a sentence of REAL rationale (readiness, endurance, assessed, leverage).
5.reflect: Why this standard, and what did you choose to leave out — and why?
5.proves: The team had to make a choice and defend it.

10.artifact: Your final common formative assessment, with a note showing which item maps to which learning target.
10.reflect: Where could a student still pass this assessment without truly learning the target?
10.proves: The assessment is shared, not solo.

13.artifact: Your CFA results broken out by learning target, plus your student sort (coded — no student names).
13.reflect: What in the data surprised you, and what does it say about our teaching — not just about the students?
13.proves: The team looked at real evidence together.

15.artifact: Your intervention plan and your extension plan for this cycle.
15.reflect: How is each part of this plan a direct response to what the Meeting 13 data showed?
15.proves: The data actually led to action.

17.artifact: Your reassessment results, showing student movement before and after (coded).
17.reflect: Who moved, who didn't, and what will you do next for students still not proficient?

18.artifact: Your completed cycle reflection and next-cycle commitment.
18.reflect: What one PLC practice will your team strengthen in the next cycle, and why that one?
18.proves: Team learning carries into the next cycle.
